lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Skill model: timeline with verified dates and requirements

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic timeline with verified dates and requirements task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Given a short model timeline where some entries are already labeled 'verified' (with a source noted) and others are labeled 'assumed,' the learner studies how each label was decided, then applies the same process to build a timeline for their own leading pathway.
safetyNotes: No real account numbers, passwords, or legal identity details are needed to complete this lesson.
materials: learner-local: notes on the learner's leading pathway from earlier units
learner-local: paper or a document for the timeline

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u06-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u06-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u06-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u06-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Pick one entry you marked 'assumed.' What specific, doable step would move it to 'verified,' and roughly when could you take that step?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u06-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u06-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u06-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Verified vs. assumed accuracy: Learner correctly distinguishes verified from assumed entries and names a real, specific source for each verified entry. | Timeline completeness: Timeline has at least four specific, dated or clearly sequenced entries relevant to the leading pathway. | Next verification step: Reflection names a specific, doable next step and a rough timeframe for taking it. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u06-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner identify which single assumed entry, if wrong, would most disrupt the rest of the timeline, and write a short plan for verifying that one first.

duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: timeline with verified dates and requirements worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Given a short model timeline where some entries are already labeled 'verified' (with a source noted) and others are labeled 'assumed,' the learner studies how each label was decided, then applies the same process to build a timeline for their own leading pathway.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact timeline with verified dates and requirements decision or action.
Model move 2: Before looking at the model, list dates or requirements you currently believe are true about your leading pathway.
Model move 3: Study the model timeline and identify what makes an entry count as 'verified' versus 'assumed.'

Model check: Verified vs. assumed accuracy: Learner correctly distinguishes verified from assumed entries and names a real, specific source for each verified entry. | Timeline completeness: Timeline has at least four specific, dated or clearly sequenced entries relevant to the leading pathway. | Next verification step: Reflection names a specific, doable next step and a rough timeframe for taking it.

resources.title: timeline with verified dates and requirements action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for timeline with verified dates and requirements.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: timeline with verified dates and requirements coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Given a short model timeline where some entries are already labeled 'verified' (with a source noted) and others are labeled 'assumed,' the learner studies how each label was decided, then applies the same process to build a timeline for their own leading pathway.
Coach direction: Before looking at the model, list dates or requirements you currently believe are true about your leading pathway.
Learner prompt: Name two dates or requirements you currently believe are true about your pathway, and be honest about whether you've actually checked them anywhere or are just assuming.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: timeline with verified dates and requirements complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Study the model timeline and identify what makes an entry count as 'verified' versus 'assumed.'
Response 1 (t2-p1): In the model timeline, what specifically makes an entry 'verified' rather than 'assumed' — what counts as a real, checkable source?

Response 2 (t2-p2): I can name at least one source (such as an official program page, a published catalog, or a direct answer from someone at the institution or organization) that would count as verification, not just a guess or something a peer said.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: timeline with verified dates and requirements minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Pick one entry you marked 'assumed.' What specific, doable step would move it to 'verified,' and roughly when could you take that step?

Success checks: Verified vs. assumed accuracy: Learner correctly distinguishes verified from assumed entries and names a real, specific source for each verified entry. | Timeline completeness: Timeline has at least four specific, dated or clearly sequenced entries relevant to the leading pathway. | Next verification step: Reflection names a specific, doable next step and a rough timeframe for taking it.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: timeline with verified dates and requirements supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u06-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u06-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional timeline with verified dates and requirements condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Verified vs. assumed accuracy: Learner correctly distinguishes verified from assumed entries and names a real, specific source for each verified entry. | Timeline completeness: Timeline has at least four specific, dated or clearly sequenced entries relevant to the leading pathway. | Next verification step: Reflection names a specific, doable next step and a rough timeframe for taking it..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u06-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: timeline with verified dates and requirements — complete fictional route

simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
